$comment: Canonical cross-repository integration lock for the Frontera runtime. Frozen by P0-PKG-02 (Protocol RC adoption) and corrected by P0-PKG-03 (self-contained artifact), and advanced in place by P0-PKG-08 (repaired Protocol candidate). P0-PKG-03 established the precedent this advance follows: when the identities or obligations the handoff binds change, the canonical current lock moves in place under a new contractVersion rather than forking a second file; superseded handoffs are recorded here, not deleted. It is the handoff PMFreak consumes next. It records identities and authorizes nothing: no registry publication, no tag, no GitHub Release, no merge. Validate the Protocol half with `node scripts/protocol/check-compatibility-lock.mjs`; reproduce the Frontera half with `npm run check:clean-room-consumer`.

This follows the attribution the 1.2.0 manifest already used for its own evidence-only follow-ups.

supersededHandoffs.notDefective: 1.2.0 is not defective and is not withdrawn for any fault of its own. Its compiled output is byte-identical to 1.2.1's. What the burn invalidated is its COMPATIBILITY EVIDENCE: it was validated and handed off against @aoc/protocol@0.2.0-rc.0, an input later declared burned. The artifact is sound; the evidence behind it was taken against a retracted input.
supersededHandoffs.consumedDownstream: PMFreak vendors this exact artifact at vendor/aoc-enterprise-runtime-1.2.0.tgz and pins it by SHA-256 in vendor/aoc-consumer.lock.json, recorded against mergeCommit a937cfb4180ec02de7b736b92039f5f8210152bc. This is the immutable, checksum-pinned consumption that makes the identity unavailable for reuse.

supersededHandoffs.note: The identity this lock recorded before this advance. Its enterprise half was deliberately held at 1.0.0 through the 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 increments because the PMFreak handoff had not yet been performed; that hold ended when PMFreak consumed 1.2.0. Retained here rather than deleted.

versioningRationale.question: Why does a Protocol repin that changes no Frontera code produce 1.2.1 rather than staying at 1.2.0?
versioningRationale.answer: Because the artifact IDENTITY moved, not the runtime semantics.
versioningRationale.measuredAgainstAnIsolatedControl: Packed in a clean POSIX (ext4) checkout, never on the /mnt/c DrvFs mount, which alters tar metadata. Control A = base commit a937cfb4 untouched, which reproduced the recorded 1.2.0 artifact byte-for-byte (sha256 1b59c63d..., 3390079 bytes), establishing the environment as canonical. Control B = the same commit with ONLY the rc.0 -> rc.1 devDependency applied and the version deliberately held at 1.2.0: sha256 4fce3405d7b753a945e642eb361b0c53e5ba051da9a31937f51c134992df232f, identical size, DIFFERENT BYTES. Both unpacked to 6366 entries with an identical file list and exactly one differing file.
findings: The runtime executable did not change: every file under dist/ is byte-identical.
The public exports did not change: 10 keys, export-map fingerprint 2b0ee1e3afee7c02d600615771eac3fa8aeec680c27bf4189041715729a22438, recomputed from the packed artifact's own package.json.
The bundled internal modules did not change: governed-authority, governed-authorization, identity and scoped-access are each byte-identical.
The frozen v1 HTTP surface did not change: release/api-surface.v1.json is byte-identical, 27 endpoints, check-api-freeze passes.
But package.json ships INSIDE the tarball, and it carries the 'file:' devDependency spec for @aoc/protocol.
So the rc.0 -> rc.1 repin changes those bytes -- the single differing file between control A and control B is package/package.json, and the single differing line is the @aoc/protocol devDependency.
An immutable 1.2.0 artifact exists and is consumed downstream, checksum-pinned by SHA-256 in PMFreak's vendor/aoc-consumer.lock.json.

Therefore reusing 1.2.0 for these different bytes would produce an artifact identity collision: one declared version naming two distinct artifacts, one of which a downstream consumer has already pinned.
1.2.1 is therefore a PATCH derived by artifact identity, not by new semantics.
versioningRationale.whyThe1_0_0PrecedentDoesNotExtend: docs/release/FRONTERA_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_1.0.0.md held the version constant across changes to dependencies and to the @aoc/protocol devDependency -- the same class of change as this one. Its stated reason was conditional: 'no repository evidence authorizes inventing 1.0.1/1.1.0, and no immutable 1.0.0 artifact exists anywhere to conflict with.' That precondition no longer holds. An immutable 1.2.0 artifact does exist, downstream, pinned by checksum. The precedent's own reasoning is what mandates the bump here.
versioningRationale.derivedNotChosen: Under this project's SemVer contract (the public HTTP API surface, the exported package entrypoints and the store schema identifiers, per docs/enterprise/API_STABILITY_V1.md) none of the three moved. A change that is neither breaking nor an additive public capability is a patch.
versioningRationale.authorizes: Nothing. No registry publication, no tag, no GitHub Release, no merge. 'private: true' is unchanged.

packageIdentityConclusion.question: Is @aoc-enterprise/runtime the canonical Frontera package PMFreak should consume?
evidence: It is the root package of Republika-Network/Frontera (package.json name = @aoc-enterprise/runtime, version 1.2.1). The repository was Soberania-Protocol/Soberania-Enterprise when this conclusion was first recorded; the rename is a GitHub-side fact and the continuity is evidenced by PMFreak's own consumer lock, which carries both slugs across the same commit chain.

It is the only package in this repository with a public exports map intended for external consumption (10 declared export keys) and a files allowlist restricting the artifact to dist plus its bundled private modules.

It is the package the repository's own release machinery targets: validate-publishability.mjs and check-clean-room-consumer.mjs pack it and install it into external consumers; check-runtime-release-integrity.mjs asserts its export targets exist; release/RELEASE_MANIFEST.json names it.

It is the identifier PMFreak actually consumes. As of P0-PKG-04/05 PMFreak vendors the packed artifact and pins it by SHA-256 in vendor/aoc-consumer.lock.json; the former file:src/aoc/enterprise specifier is now on that lock's forbiddenSpecifiers list and the local copy directories are recorded as REMOVED. Verified by reading PMFreak read-only; PMFreak was not modified.
As of P0-PKG-03 it is self-contained: a clean external consumer installing only this artifact and the Protocol candidate loads all ten declared exports.
packageIdentityConclusion.relationshipToAocEnterprise: @aoc/enterprise is a DIFFERENT, unrelated package: a private:true Assurance workspace living at enterprise/ inside the Soberania_Protocol repository, version 0.1.0, with its own ./assurance/* export map. It is not an alias of @aoc-enterprise/runtime, is not built by this repository, and is not the PMFreak handoff.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The measured closure from the ten public export entry points is four private workspace packages (governed-authority, governed-authorization, identity, scoped-access) -- P0-PKG-02's figure of 13 came from grepping all of dist including modules no export reaches. All four now travel inside the artifact as npm bundleDependencies, remain private:true, and are asserted present, real (non-symlink) and private by check:clean-room-consumer on every run. /kernel, /enterprise and /kernel-host load externally. The superseded blocked candidate (sha256 93b9d9f1...5c1c30f8, commit 65db731e...) is recorded in release/frontera-candidate-manifest-1.0.0.json under superseded_candidate.

pmfreakObligations: PMFreak must repin from @aoc-enterprise/runtime@1.2.0 to the exact successor artifact identified above, by SHA-256, and from the BURNED @aoc/protocol@0.2.0-rc.0 to 0.2.0-rc.1. This is the live obligation this advance creates; it is downstream work that this increment neither performs nor authorizes.
PMFreak must consume the exact frozen Frontera artifact identified above, by SHA-256.
DISCHARGED by PMFreak P0-PKG-04/05: stop using file:src/aoc/enterprise. Its consumer lock now lists that specifier as forbidden and records the local copy as REMOVED.
DISCHARGED by PMFreak P0-PKG-04/05: stop using file:src/aoc/protocol and install the pinned @aoc/protocol candidate instead.
PMFreak must not copy Frontera source.
PMFreak must not reinterpret Protocol contracts through local copies.
PMFreak must import only through declared export keys of each package.
PMFreak must not install, declare or depend on any private @aoc-enterprise/* implementation module -- they are internal to the Frontera artifact.
PMFreak must record repository, commit, version and SHA-256 of every installed artifact in its own consumer lock file.
PMFreak must run a blocking CI job that reinstalls the pinned artifacts (npm ci) and re-runs its consumer battery.
